summary: H.R. 3495, titled the Direct Seller and Real Estate Agent Harmonization Act, amends the Fair Labor Standards Act of 1938 to explicitly exclude direct sellers of consumer products and qualified real estate agents from the definition of an "employee." Consequently, these workers would not be covered by federal requirements guaranteeing minimum wage and overtime compensation under that law.

affected_groups.effect: Excluded from the Fair Labor Standards Act definition of employee, meaning they are not subject to its minimum wage and overtime rules.

key_provisions: Amends Section 3(e) of the Fair Labor Standards Act of 1938.
Excludes direct sellers from the definition of an employee.
Excludes qualified real estate agents from the definition of an employee.
Uses definitions for direct sellers and qualified real estate agents as set forth in section 3508(b) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986.

summary_detail.plain_summary: H.R. 3495, titled the Direct Seller and Real Estate Agent Harmonization Act, amends the Fair Labor Standards Act of 1938 to explicitly exclude direct sellers of consumer products and qualified real estate agents from the definition of an "employee." Consequently, these workers would not be covered by federal requirements guaranteeing minimum wage and overtime compensation under that law.
summary_detail.significance: The bill alters labor standards protections by clarifying that specific categories of independent-style workers—direct sellers and real estate agents—do not qualify as employees under federal wage and hour laws, removing them from standard minimum wage and overtime mandates.
